randomness.name: Randomness: What Can Chance Change?
randomness.description: A draw enters a world that has already made choices: its possible values, their distribution, the eligible bodies, the clock, the memory and the consequences. Begin by recovering a picture, then discover how the same draw can become a colour, an absence, a step, a garment or a lost foothold. Learning those rules also makes it possible to ask which other bodies and relations they could admit.
randomness.qfep_connection: The sequence investigates the project’s connection between uncertainty, possibility and freedom through specific encounters. Empirical categorical Shannon entropy measures symbol shares in a retained sample; it is not a direct measure of spatial disorder, thermodynamic entropy or freedom. The critical question remains open: which differences may occur within a rule, and what changes when we alter the rule itself?
learning_objectives: Separate a generator seed from the procedure that consumes and assigns its draws
Compare sample order, symbol shares and categorical Shannon entropy without equating them
Inspect eligibility before selection, then distinguish hiding geometry from withdrawing collision support
Relate local binary marks to larger contours and a separately implemented navigation graph
Compare a physical-looking die outcome with a retained record and the conditions of its throws
Separate accumulated changes in position, orientation and appearance
Distinguish direction sets, bounded step-length laws, boundary handling and retained history
Compare sampling procedures, clipping and rebinning of the same stored values
Distinguish variation within a wardrobe from changing the construction that makes forms possible
Compare independent spatial variation with correlated neighbours and finite layered fields
Identify the different jobs of chance in mark generation, numerical estimation, path growth and particle updates
Compare a recorded trail with a signal that influences later choices
Distinguish an already sampled deadline from an undrawn wait, and a cue from the event it reveals

artifact_groups.rationale: Recover a seeded picture, then compare how other devices produce or retain a draw.
The board defines eligibility; paired cases compare returning and withholding a member; the floor connects removal to bodily support.

Take one line of BASIC apart at its coin (205.5) and its semicolon, see the same stream laid on the floor, then walk into twelve of its characters stood up as solid walls to find whether they left a way through.
Read one throw, then combine two physical faces into one coloured column; compare the coin, changing heap and bounded field.
Random transformations on geometric objects; introduces entropy decay concept
Follow accumulated steps in the central terrarium, then compare paper traces, a leash and a self-avoiding path.
Compare retained samples at the central cabinet; falling beads, three sampling laws and paint marks extend that comparison.
Follow three existing encounters: sampled specimens, an arrival wardrobe and altered garment constructions. The bubble dish remains a supporting population.
Random geometric transformations at structural level; environment-scale sculpting
Gallery of artistic randomness applications: Pollock, Monte Carlo, pipe systems
Stigmergy and pheromone trails: randomness leaving traces becomes emergent behavior
Compare a finite sine-based field mixer with retained cellular, spatial and statistical representations. No claim that the mixer simulates geology.
The central crossing samples waits; a separate rear bay samples falling-cube positions and velocities. Both remain book encounters.
Measure symbol shares at the central ledger; compare the measurement with visible disorder in the side exhibits.

learning_objectives: Entropy as possibility space, not destruction
PRNG vs TRNG: deterministic sequences vs physical randomness

Shannon entropy: H = -Σ p log p. Logarithm measures disorder. Factorials count arrangements. The integral named at change (seq 4.5) reappears here as expectation — sum over a distribution becomes integral in the continuous limit.
